name: BlahDNS Browser Extension 0.2.2 preview
body:
BlahDNS Browser Extension 0.2.2 completes structural checks for cosmetic selectors and adds enabled-proxy status assertions to the permanent browser suite.

- The background parser rejects unclosed quotes, brackets and parentheses, mismatched closers, trailing escapes, CSS newline controls and existing comment delimiters. Supported quoted delimiters and valid escapes remain accepted. Invalid selectors are diagnosed before CSS generation, so later valid rules remain effective. These are bounded structural checks, not full CSS grammar validation.
- After enabling each HTTP and SOCKS5 fixture proxy, the browser suite calls getState and requires proxyStatus.applied=true before verifying actual routed requests. Exact PAC comparison is unchanged.

Verified: 56 unit tests, 252 expectations and 21 integration checks each in Chrome, Brave and Firefox. The new selector tests first reproduced the original failure, then passed after the fix. Existing readonly native status, WebRTC/RFP, filtering scopes, WebSocket, settings round-trip, themes and default-list updates remain passing. Repeated local builds produce identical ZIP/XPI hashes.

Downloads: Chromium ZIP, Firefox ZIP, unsigned Firefox XPI and SHA256SUMS. Firefox ZIP/XPI are byte-identical. Chrome/Brave use Load unpacked with the extracted Chromium ZIP. Firefox uses about:debugging → Load Temporary Add-on with the intact XPI or the extracted manifest.json. Temporary Firefox installs end at restart; ordinary permanent installation requires Mozilla signing.

No new dependency, permission, telemetry or settings-schema change. Prior tags/assets are preserved. Full evidence is in docs/evals/0.2.2/.
